title: Root cause & remediation for customer-reported overage: anomalous metering vs rate-limit behavior
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Summary: A strategic-account customer (AcctID: redacted) filed an overage dispute reporting 3x expected token consumption in their March billing window. Support escalated to eng after initial QA found discrepancy between customer telemetry and our Usage Ledger. This ticket captures investigation logs, immediate mitigations, root-cause hypothesis, and recommended customer remediation (credits + config changes).

Scope and goals:
- Verify accuracy of Redwood usage accounting for the customer’s API key across the disputed window (2026-02-26 to 2026-03-02).
- Determine whether rate limiting or quota enforcement failed, allowing unintended burst/bypass.
- Identify any edge cases in batching, prefix/KV cache accounting, or meter aggregation that could overcount tokens.
- Propose data-backed credit amount and long-term fixes (runtime guards, observability alerts, billing reconciliation tooling).

Data sources examined:
- Usage Ledger (postgres), tokenized request logs (s3/redwood-telemetry/2026-02/), API gateway request traces (traces:gw-prod), per-model runtime counters (prometheus:runtime.tokens_emitted), rate-limiter audit logs (kafka:rl-audit), customer-provided app logs (support attachment), and customer billing report.

Investigation timeline & findings (high level):
- 2026-03-01: Support intake flagged a 3x spike compared to historical baseline; created support case SC-5478.
- 2026-03-02: Quick QA: verified Usage Ledger shows same gross tokens used as billing invoice. No immediate DB corruption.
- 2026-03-03: Reproduced a synthetic workload matching customer pattern: heavy short-lived parallel chat sessions with streaming enabled. Observed higher per-session token accounting when streaming and continuous batching combined.
- 2026-03-04: Correlated rate-limiter audit logs: rate-limiter allowed bursts (token bucket refill math) while the API gateway returned 429 at application layer for a minority of requests. Several requests were retried by customer SDK; retries were counted as separate usages.
- 2026-03-05: Found a logic gap: when streaming responses are closed by the client mid-response, runtime emits final tokens into the ledger twice in rare race conditions (kv-cache flush + stream finalizer both reported emission). This occurred ~0.8% of sessions in synthetic test with identical timing.

Root causes (combined):
1) Accounting duplication during stream finalization: under specific timing, the runtime double-reported emitted tokens for the same generation. Reproducible in stress tests.
2) Client-side retry behavior: the customer SDK retried idempotent calls without exponential backoff, causing repeated billable requests. Our rate limiter allowed short burst retries because the burst window and per-key quota were permissive for dedicated customers.
3) Observability gap: no alert for per-key token-once-anomalies nor reconciliation pipeline between runtime counters and ledger entries (we only alert on gross monthly delta thresholds).

Impact estimate:
- Direct overcount from duplication: ~12% of the measured overage (~approx 360k tokens of 3M disputed tokens).
- Retry amplification: estimated 45% of disputed increment due to retries (repeated full prompt + response cycles).
- Remaining delta likely legitimate usage (new workload) and customer misunderstanding of streaming token model: ~43%.

Immediate mitigations applied (temporary):
- 2026-03-06: Runtime patch v1 applied to production edge: add a dedupe key for emission finalizer events for 10s window. Patch ID: PR#re-1123. Rollout to 20% then 100% in 4 hours.
- 2026-03-06: Rate-limiter config adjusted for account to reduce burst allowance and turn on stricter per-key retry-window enforcement (config change cfg-rl-241).
- 2026-03-07: Support communicated to customer with interim goodwill credit (see Credits section) and guidance on disabling aggressive client retries and properly closing streams.

Proposed customer remediation:
- Offer credit equal to the portion of overage attributable to system duplication + a goodwill discount on retry amplification portion while we complete further validation. Proposed credit: $3,250 (approx 60% of disputed invoice delta). Reasoning: duplication is provable; retry amplification partially their SDK behavior but we accepted partial responsibility given permissive burst settings and lack of explicit guidance.
- Provide a technical writeup and runbook for the customer’s engineering team describing streaming semantics and recommended SDK configuration (attach runbook link).

Long-term fixes and follow-ups (owner assignments):
- ENG-8973 (Marco): Comprehensive dedupe-and-idempotency layer in runtime emission pipeline (estimate 13 pts).
- ENG-8980 (Observability): Build reconciliation job that compares runtime.prometheus counters against ledger ingestion per-key nightly and surfaces >2% drift alerts with automated tickets.
- ENG-9005 (Billing): Add per-request UUID field to ledger entries to make head-to-head de-duplication feasible during dispute investigations.
- PM action (Lena): Update docs and SDKs with explicit retry guidance for streaming and add a centralized billing FAQ article.

Open questions:
- How to handle historical customers who used older SDK versions that may have retried without backoff? (scope policy decision).
- Should burst allowances be tightened globally or exist as account-level opt-in?

Artifacts and links:
- Support case: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SC-5478
- Runtime patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/re-1123
- Test harness used: s3://redwood-tests/stream-dup-repro/2026-03-03/ (internal)
- Reconciliation dashboard (slice): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/billing/recon/account/REDACTED
- Customer communication (sent): drive://support/credits/SC-5478/letter-2026-03-07.md

Acceptance criteria to close this ticket:
- Root cause fully documented and reproducible test case checked into runtime tests.
- Permanent dedupe fix merged and deployed with no regression in throughput (tracked by canary dashboards).
- Reconciliation job deployed to staging and alerts created for affected accounts.
- Customer credit approved by Finance and applied; confirmation sent to customer and support case closed with postmortem attached.
